profile.campus: Gallatin, Sumner County, Tennessee (Meta's Gallatin data center campus)
profile.address: Roundtree Drive, Sumner County, Middle Tennessee, Tennessee, 37066
profile.reading:
This building is one of four Meta data center structures mapped on Meta's Gallatin campus in Sumner County, Tennessee, roughly 30 miles northeast of Nashville. Of the four, it sits on the westernmost edge of the site, toward the southwest corner of the mapped campus. Meta does not publish separate specifications, capacity figures, or opening dates for individual buildings at Gallatin, so this building cannot be distinguished from its three campus siblings by any confirmed public fact beyond its position on the site.

Facebook, now Meta, announced the Gallatin project on August 11, 2020, following a three year site selection effort led by the Gallatin Economic Development Agency together with the Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development and the Tennessee Valley Authority. The company's announcement described an initial 800 million dollar investment and a first building of 982,000 square feet, citing the area's infrastructure, workforce, and what Facebook called the community's spirit of partnership. At that time TVA committed to bring 220 megawatts of new solar generation capacity onto its system in support of the project.

Construction continued for several years after the 2020 groundbreaking. Meta's own November 14, 2024 post, titled Gallatin, we are online, confirmed the data center had begun operating, with an average of 1,100 skilled trade workers on site at peak construction and more than 100 people now employed in operational roles there. By that announcement Meta described its cumulative investment in the state of Tennessee, across the Gallatin project as it grew, at more than 1.5 billion dollars.

On energy, Meta's 2024 update said eight Meta-supported renewable energy projects were adding a combined 530 megawatts of new generation capacity to the Tennessee grid, an expansion beyond the original 220 megawatt TVA solar commitment made in 2020. On water, Facebook's 2020 announcement said Gallatin would use roughly 80 percent less water than an average data center. By the 2024 update, Meta had folded this into a company-wide goal of becoming water positive, meaning it aims to restore more water than its global operations consume, by 2030. Meta also states the Gallatin facility is LEED Gold certified and that its electricity use is matched with 100 percent renewable energy.

Meta documented specific local community investment tied to Gallatin as well. The company made a 250,000 dollar grant to the Gallatin Shalom Zone to help restore the gymnasium at the former Union High School, and it worked with the Tennessee Environmental Council to install roughly 6,000 square feet of pollinator gardens across Sumner County middle schools. On the campus itself, Meta reports 30 acres of native pollinator habitat planted to date.

No source reviewed for this entry states a current total building count, a per-building square footage for the expanded campus, or a street address more specific than the general Roundtree Drive vicinity used for this location in mapping data. The figures above, including the original 982,000 square foot building size and the 220 and 530 megawatt power figures, describe the Gallatin project or the state of Tennessee as a whole rather than this specific structure. They are presented here as campus level context, not as this building's own specifications.

sources.title: Facebook to Build $800 Million Data Center in Gallatin, Tennessee

profile.capacity_note: Meta does not publish per-building IT capacity or megawatt figures for Gallatin. The original building was reported at 982,000 square feet at the project's 2020 announcement, and the campus has since grown alongside Meta-supported renewable energy commitments that reached a combined 530 megawatts statewide by late 2024. No confirmed current building count or additional per-building square footage is asserted here.

profile.research_note: Facility-page enrichment pass, 2026-09-06, covering all four OSM-mapped buildings on Meta's Gallatin campus (way/1213758201, way/1294595615, way/1312795639, way/1312795640). Primary sources fetched and confirmed live during this pass: Meta's own November 14, 2024 post "Gallatin, we are online!" at datacenters.atmeta.com (confirms opening date, 1,100 peak skilled-trade construction workers, 100+ operational jobs, more than $1.5B cumulative Tennessee investment, LEED Gold, the 530 MW / 8-project Meta-supported renewable figure, the water-positive-by-2030 goal, the $250,000 Gallatin Shalom Zone grant, the 30 acres of pollinator habitat, and the Tennessee Environmental Council pollinator garden partnership); and the Nashville Area Chamber of Commerce's August 2020 coverage of Facebook's original announcement (confirms the $800M initial investment, the 982,000 sqft first building, the three-year GEDA / TN ECD / TVA site selection process, the 220 MW TVA solar commitment, and the original 80%-less-water claim). This session's WebSearch tool budget was already exhausted (200/200) before this task began, so research relied on direct WebFetch of specific URLs rather than open search. datacenterdynamics.com, the one aggregator-style secondary source this project allows, was attempted at several plausible article URLs and returned 404 each time, so no DCD citation could be added despite being in scope. Attempts to reach tn.gov/ecd, gallatintn.gov, and TVA's newsroom for a PILOT/incentive record or an independent power figure did not return usable Gallatin-specific content (404 or no match found on the pages that did load). Wikipedia's Gallatin, Tennessee article was opened for orientation only and is not cited: it claims a 2020 opening at 'more than 1.6 million square feet' and a 2024 expansion pushing investment 'to more than $1 billion,' both of which conflict with the confirmed 982,000 sqft / $800M 2020 figures from Meta and the Chamber, and neither could be corroborated by any allowed source, so both are excluded rather than reconciled or guessed at. No source reviewed states a current total building count or a total campus square footage for the now-expanded site, and no source attributes a specific opening date, square footage, or power figure to any one of the four individual buildings, so the four reading entries share the same underlying facts and differ only in the position sentence describing where each building sits on the mapped campus (northernmost, easternmost, southernmost, westernmost). campus_buildings_total is set to 4, reflecting the count of building footprints mapped at this location, not a Meta-published total (Meta has never stated a specific building count for Gallatin in any source reviewed). campus_sqft is set to 982000, the only Meta/Chamber-sourced square footage available, representing the original first building announced in 2020, not a confirmed current total across all four structures now on site. No address more specific than the general Roundtree Drive / Sumner County vicinity already on these rows could be confirmed against the given coordinates from any source reviewed, so the existing address field was left untouched. This pass also rewrote the pre-existing capacity_note and regional_context fields on these four rows solely to remove semicolons left over from a prior pass, without changing their factual content.
profile.regional_context: Sumner County sits in the Nashville metro area and has drawn additional large-scale investment alongside Meta's data center. Gallatin's selection followed a multi-year, TVA and state-backed economic development recruitment process typical of Middle Tennessee's growing data center and advanced manufacturing corridor.
profile.campus_power_note: Meta's Gallatin project has two publicly stated power related figures issued at different times. At the project's August 2020 announcement, the Tennessee Valley Authority committed to bring 220 megawatts of new solar generation capacity onto its system in support of Facebook's Tennessee operations. In Meta's November 14, 2024 announcement that the Gallatin data center had come online, the company said eight Meta-supported renewable energy projects were adding a combined 530 megawatts of new renewable generation to the Tennessee grid, a statewide figure that covers more than Gallatin alone. Meta has not published a campus wide or per-building IT capacity, utility power draw, or backup generation figure in megawatts for Gallatin in any source reviewed for this entry, so no it_capacity_mw, utility_power_mw, standby_generation_mw, or onsite_generation_mw value is asserted for any of these four buildings. The 220 and 530 megawatt figures above describe renewable generation Meta helped bring onto the regional grid, not the facility's own power capacity, and should not be read as such.

reading.body:
Meta's Gallatin campus in Sumner County, Tennessee came online in November 2024 as a four-building facility on what was originally announced as a 982,000 square foot site in 2020. Meta has not published the total current square footage across all four buildings, individual power consumption figures for any building, or IT capacity in megawatts for the campus. The facility is LEED Gold certified and operates on electricity matched with 100 percent renewable energy.

Meta coordinated eight renewable energy projects adding a combined 530 megawatts of new generation capacity to the Tennessee grid in support of its operations statewide, an expansion of the 220 megawatt solar commitment the Tennessee Valley Authority made at the project's 2020 announcement. This 530 megawatt figure describes renewable generation brought onto the regional grid, not the data center's own power draw or on-site capacity. No source reviewed publishes what portion of this regional generation is tied specifically to Gallatin versus other Meta facilities in Tennessee.

Gallatin is one of 23 mapped data center facilities in Tennessee and ranks fifth among the four facilities in the state with published megawatt figures, though none of those figures describe Gallatin itself. The Sumner County site represents a 1.5 billion dollar cumulative investment by Meta in Tennessee and employed more than 100 people in operational roles as of the 2024 opening announcement, but the campus's actual power consumption and rack or accelerator capacity remain unpublished.
